Pilot card · Grixis · Tier 2 · Proxy · Lane B
 The Hundred Million Shattered Jewels
 Ichioku Gyokusai
 MARCHESA, THE BLACK ROSE
 U B R 
 printed: Ishiwara Kanji, the Unauthorized War
 Dethrone. Other creatures you control have dethrone.
 Whenever a creature you control with a +1/+1 counter on it dies, return that card to the battlefield under your control at the beginning of the next end step.
 Dethrone: attacks the player with the most life (or tied) → +1/+1 counter.
 3/3 
 ↻ The value turn — from turn 5, every turn
 1
 Steal the best creature
 Mark of Mutiny (adds its own counter), Traitorous Greed (+2 mana), Captivating Crew ({3}{R}, main phase only), Conscripts, The Beast, Scepter, Dihada −3.
 2
 Swing at the life leader
 Dethrone puts the counter on. Steal from anyone, attack whoever has the most life. That counter is the conversion — the steal alone is Act of Treason.
 3
 Sacrifice after combat
 Viscera Seer, Carrion Feeder, Phyrexian Altar, Ashnod's Altar, Goblin Bombardment , or Phyrexian Tower / High Market.
 4
 It comes back yours
 End step, permanently. On the way in: Terror / Warstorm Surge deal its power to any target, Purphoros 2 to each opponent, Tremors 1 to each.
 5
 Stay off the top
 Never be the sole life leader — dethrone goes dead. Zulaport and Bastion gain you life. Spend it: Spirit Over Steel, Deluge, Night's Whisper, Arena.
 No counter? Convert: 
 Mark of Mutiny — built in › 
 Unspeakable Symbol — 3 life › 
 Professor's Warning — instant › 
 Kaya's Ghostform — none needed 
 Rules that decide games
 - "Under your control," not its owner's. Stolen, countered, and dies while yours: it's yours for the rest of the game.
 - Marchesa brings herself back. She dies with a counter → decline the command zone , leave her in the yard, she returns at the end step.
 - Tokens never return. Siege-Gang's and Beetleback's Goblins, Snakes, Faeries: fodder only.
 - "The next end step." Sacrifice before it begins: back this turn. Dies during it (Slave of Bolas): back a turn later.
 - Sweep after you attack. Toxic Deluge after a dethrone combat is one-sided — everything with a counter comes back yours.
 Mulligan
 3+ lands and a cheap outlet or rock: keep.
 Seer, Feeder, Sol Ring, Signet/Talisman, Bitterblossom, Skullclamp. Ship two-landers without Sol Ring and all-steal hands with no outlet. She's in the zone every game — don't keep for her.
 Traps — each one costs you the creature
 - Stealing a commander: it dies to the command zone, nothing comes back. Steal it to attack with, not to keep.
 - Progenitus, Vigor, Kozilek shuffle away. Use them, don't sacrifice them.
 - Evacuation (The Jewel Voice Broadcast) sends creatures to their owners' hands — your stolen army goes home. Never after a big Mob Rule turn.
 - Slip Out the Back on a stolen creature ends the steal. Marchesa only.
 - Kill turn: keep a free outlet up in case they kill the Altar.
 How you win — a two-turn kill
 Mob Rule

 all of them, post-combat

 = their power
 Terror, at end step. They're yours.
 16 MANA
6 ON THE TURN 
 Already down: Marchesa, an outlet, Terror of the Peaks (The Hundred Million Shattered Jewels) . Against Justice's dinosaurs (~36 power) that's one player dead in combat, a second at the end step, and next turn you attack with the table's army.
 Protect her through the end step. Kill Marchesa in response to the return trigger and every return fails . Boots, Slip Out the Back, Professor's Warning, Fierce Guardianship (free while she's out).
 Backups: Insurrection (8, everything), Mass Mutiny (5, one per opponent), Hideous Taskmaster (7, steals on cast — lands even if countered). Drain per creature, per cycle: Purphoros + Tremors = 9 off the table on re-entry, and neither gains you life.
 At this table
 Justice · Kenrith dinos
 He's the ammunition: power 4+ bodies, and lifegain keeps him leader. Kill Seedborn Muse first. Into open {W}{U}, lead with Taskmaster or The Beast — Dovin's Veto can't hit creatures.
 Conqueror's Flail · Vigor
 Flail on sight: Bedevil, Kolaghan's Command, Chaos Warp, or steal it with Conscripts. With Vigor out, point Terror at players only.
 Avery · Anti-Venom
 No drain reaches 1,700. Take the machine — Mob Rule ignores life totals, and he's always the leader, so dethrone always has a target.
 Drannith · nothing to steal
 Drannith stops Marchesa from the zone (self-return still works) — kill or steal it. Knowledge Pool, K'rrik: no second kill; interaction and Disrupt Decorum keep you alive.
 Before the
first shuffle
 Heads up — this is the Supernova in the East deck, Imperial Japan through 1945. It steals your armies, and some of the cards are the bad stuff on purpose. Tell me if it lands wrong and I'll table it. 
 Then actually table it if asked. Don't defend the design mid-game.
